summary: Kristin Johnston Largen works in religious and Buddhist studies. In 2018, she was attested as Professor of Systematic Theology at United Lutheran Seminary and Associate Dean of Religious and Spiritual Life at Gettysburg College.

Kristin Scheible specializes in Buddhist and religious studies. She studied at Colby College and Harvard University under Anne E. Monius, Diana L. Eck, John S. Strong, and Charles Hallisey, later holding teaching positions at Harvard, Brown, and Bard College.

Kristina Myrvold works in religious studies and Indology. She studied as a doctoral candidate and worked as an editor at Lund University, and was attested as Assistant Professor of Religious Studies at Linnaeus University in 2014.

Kristofer Schipper (1934–2021) was a sinologist and religious studies scholar. Educated in Paris, his career included posts at the École Française d'Extrême-Orient, École Pratique des Hautes Études, CNRS, Collège de France, Leiden University, and Fuzhou University.

Krisztina Teleki is a scholar of Central Asian studies, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. She earned her MA at Eötvös Loránd University between 2002 and 2009, and was a research fellow there around 2010.
Kshanika Saha is a scholar in Buddhist studies who completed her PhD at the University of Calcutta under the supervision of Nalinaksha Dutt, attested in 1966.

Kshetresa Chandra Chattopadhyaya (1896–1974) was an Indologist and linguist. Educated at Calcutta, Presidency, Allahabad, and Sampurnanand Sanskrit universities under Ganganatha Jha, he held posts at Allahabad, Sampurnanand Sanskrit University, Rashtriya Sanskrit Vidyapeetha, and Calcutta.

Kshitimohan Sen (1880–1960) was a scholar of Indology and religious studies who earned his M.A. at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University. He worked for Chamba State's Department of Education before his long tenure at Visva-Bharati University.
Kumar Shrestha works in Indology, history, and archaeology. In 2018, he was attested at the National Archives of Nepal and as an editorial board member of Documenta Nepalica.

Kumataro Kawada (1899–1981) was a philosopher and Buddhist studies scholar educated at the University of Tokyo. He held professorships at Japan Women's University, Tokyo University of Literature and Science, the University of Tokyo, and Komazawa University.

Kun Chang (1917–2017) was a linguist, sinologist, and Tibetologist. He studied at Tsinghua and Yale under Franklin Edgerton and Geshe Ngawang Nyima, holding posts at Academia Sinica, the University of Washington, and UC Berkeley.

Kunio Harikai is a scholar of Indology and philosophy who completed his BA and PhD degrees at Kyushu University under Seiren Matsunami and Shoren Ihara. He served as Associate Professor at Saga Medical School from around 1978 to 1993.
Kunio Iwaya studied at the University of Tokyo from around 1962 to 1971 and held an academic post at Meiji Gakuin University from approximately 1976 to 2014.
Kunio Mugitani is a scholar of Sinology and philosophy. He studied under Mitsuji Fukunaga and served as a professor at Kyoto University from around 1993 to 2012.

Kunio Odaka (1908–1993) studied at the University of Tokyo from around 1928 to 1931. He held academic posts at the University of Tokyo from around 1945 to 1969 and at Sophia University from around 1969 to 1979.

Kunio Yanagita (1875–1962) was a Japanology and religious studies scholar educated at the University of Tokyo. He worked for government ministries, the League of Nations Permanent Mandates Commission, and held posts at Keio and Kokugakuin universities.

Kuno Fischer (1824–1907) was a German philosopher who studied at the universities of Leipzig and Halle-Wittenberg. He held professorial posts at the University of Jena from around 1856 to 1872 and at Heidelberg University from 1850 to 1907.

Kuno Lorenz is a philosopher educated at Tübingen, Hamburg, Bonn, Princeton, Kiel, and Erlangen-Nürnberg. He held a chair in philosophy at the University of Hamburg in 1970 and served as professor at Saarland University from 1974 to 1998.

Kuno Meyer (1858–1919) was a linguist who studied under Ernst Windisch at the University of Leipzig. He held academic posts at the University of Liverpool from around 1884 to 1911 and at the University of Berlin from 1911 to 1915.

Kuntala Bhattacharya is a scholar of philosophy and Buddhist studies. She studied under Prabal Kumar Sen, Shyamapada Misra, and Amita Chatterjee at Jadavpur University, and held a post at Rabindra Bharati University attested in 2009.
